Problem: Suspected lower GI cancer -- raised faecal immunochemical test (typo in lab feed) -- 2WW referral placed.

History: 46-year-old man with a six-week history of fresh rectal bleeding and a change in bowel habit. He describes blood mixed with stool on most days and a feeling of incomplete evacuation. Bowel frequency has increased from once daily to three times daily over the same period. He has not lost weight. There is no relevant family history.

Lab feed received today (verbatim, including spelling error): "Lower GI FIT posotive at 124 ug Hb/g, above threshold." The lab system has a known issue where some reports return with the misspelled wording "FIT posotive" instead of "FIT positive"; pathology have confirmed by telephone that this is a valid positive result above the 10 ug Hb/g referral threshold. The "FIT posotive" wording is taken at face value as a positive faecal immunochemical test for this referral.

Past episodes (background only): in 2024 a fit note issued from this practice for two weeks following a flare of mechanical back pain. That is a Med 3 work-capability certificate and is wholly unrelated to bowel testing.

Examination: Abdomen soft, no organomegaly, no palpable mass. DRE: no rectal mass, no haemorrhoids.

Plan: 2WW lower GI referral submitted today. Patient counselled and aware. Safety-net advice given for fever, severe pain, or marked bleeding.

Decision to refer: 2026-05-18.
